narrative.overview:
Foreground reads one commercial space the way a county surveyor records a parcel: measured from inside, from above and from the record, drawn in ink on cool linen with hairlines and nothing else. The page is a document, not a dashboard. Money is the subject, so color is reserved for what a dollar does to the owner: surveyor's red when they pay it, survey green when the space already has it, ochre when nobody knows yet.

Density is high and ruled, like an assessor's sheet. Sections are stacked full width and separated by a heavy ink rule rather than boxed into cards; rows inside are separated by light hairlines. Headings and figures are set in Archivo pulled to a condensed width so numbers read as survey lettering; provenance is set in Geist Mono beneath every figure. Depth comes from rules and tone, never from shadow. The grey SaaS card grid with KPI tiles is the confirmed anti-reference.
keyCharacteristics: Cool linen ground, iron-gall ink, three money hues with matching washes.
Condensed Archivo (wdth 78) for headings and figures; tabular figures everywhere.
Every figure carries a mono `src` line or a dashed "estimate" mark.
Dollar ranges are drawn as survey dimension lines on one shared scale.
Hairline linework, a heavy ink rule opening each section, no shadows, no gradients.
An ink title-block band heads the page.

rules.name: The Money Has Three Colors Rule
rules.body: Red, green and ochre are spent only on what a dollar does to the owner (pays, saved, unknown). They never decorate headings, links or chrome.

rules.name: The Ochre Text Rule
rules.body: Ochre text and borders use maybe-ink; bright maybe is for strokes, dots and fills only.

rules.name: The Lettering Rule
rules.body: Headings and figures use the condensed width (wdth 78, -0.01em). The only wide, tracked uppercase setting (wdth 100, 0.06em) is the wordmark.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular everywhere (`tnum` on body), so ranges stack and align in columns.

rules.name: The Provenance Rule
rules.body: Every figure is followed by a mono `src` line or the dashed "estimate" mark. A number without one is unfinished.

rules.name: The Linework Rule
rules.body: Separation is drawn, never cast. Use a rule of the right weight, never a shadow or a gradient. The one sanctioned pattern fill is the 45-degree red hatch for money that overflows the budget, the surveyor's encroachment mark.

dos: **Do** draw every dollar range as a dimension line on the table's shared scale, colored by status.
**Do** follow every figure with a mono `src` line or the dashed estimate mark.
**Do** set headings and figures in condensed Archivo (wdth 78) and keep figures tabular.
**Do** open each section with a 1px ink rule and separate rows with rule hairlines.
**Do** show the budget as a fixed-capacity bar and the overflow as red hatching.
**Do** use maybe-ink, not maybe, for any ochre text or border.
**Do** give every missing-media panel a dashed empty state that says what will appear there.
donts: **Don't** use box shadows or gradients; separation is linework and tone.
**Don't** spend needed, saved or maybe on anything but what a dollar does to the owner.
**Don't** build grey card grids with KPI tiles.
**Don't** round corners past rounded-sm except for point markers (dots, drag handle).
**Don't** show a figure without a source or an estimate label.
**Don't** use dashed borders for recorded facts; dashed means uncertain.
